profilePeriod: Chancellorship, November 2005–December 2021, with greater weight on the later governing record and explicit earlier context.

sources.title: Merkel speech on federalism reform
sources.evidence: Supported returning legislative responsibilities to Länder, clearer division of powers, and joint educational evaluation; federalism includes national responsibilities.

sources.title: Merkel on the first free Volkskammer election
sources.evidence: Commemorated free elections and rejection of SED rule; parliamentary representation, freedom and pluralism are foundational.

sources.title: Policy statement by Chancellor Merkel
sources.evidence: Defends social market economy, employers and unions, balanced budgets, regulated finance, minimum wage with employment safeguards, social insurance and nuclear exit.

sources.title: Germany is a country of freedom
sources.evidence: Rejects unlimited technically possible surveillance; security is bounded by law and proportionality.

sources.title: Emergency brake to be rigorously applied
sources.evidence: Merkel and Länder leaders agreed restrictions and possible curfews in high-incidence districts.

sources.title: Constitutional Court on federal emergency brake
sources.evidence: Court upheld time-limited federal pandemic curfews/contact restrictions; national coordination coexisted with constitutional judicial scrutiny.

sources.title: Federation-Länder decision
sources.evidence: Final-period government supported stronger restrictions and a parliamentary decision on compulsory vaccination; do not mistake a proposed mandate for an enacted universal mandate.

sources.title: Merkel gegen Legalisierung von Cannabis (dpa)
sources.evidence: Direct Merkel interview rejects recreational legalisation while retaining limited medical use.

sources.title: Focus on participation
sources.evidence: Integration requires German language and constitutional values, alongside participation and belonging in an immigration society.

sources.title: Merkel refugee policy statement
sources.evidence: Combines protection and integration of genuine refugees with external borders, faster asylum procedures and returns for those without residence prospects.

sources.title: Merkel Munich Security Conference speech
sources.evidence: Supports NATO, European defence, Lithuania deployment, engagement in Iraq and careful Afghanistan policy; proposes UN Chapter VII support against terrorism.

sources.title: Making the case for free trade
sources.evidence: Calls protectionism and isolationism damaging to competition and innovation; favours openness and coordinated global rules.

sources.title: Franco-German recovery initiative
sources.evidence: Joint Merkel-Macron initiative proposes EU borrowing financing grants, an exceptional fiscal response rather than permanent state planning.

sources.title: Draghi farewell remarks
sources.evidence: Draghi specifically credits Merkel with consistently defending central-bank independence despite political pressure.

sources.title: Merkel speech on Reformation anniversary
sources.evidence: Values Christian roots, faith and social responsibility while explicitly defending religious neutrality of the state and equal freedom of belief.

sources.title: Reuters: Merkel voted against gay marriage
sources.evidence: Voted against marriage equality because she regarded marriage as male-female, while welcoming respect and social cohesion after its passage.

sources.title: Bundestag beschließt Ehe für alle (epd/KNA)
sources.evidence: Reports her changed support for adoption by same-sex couples despite opposing the marriage bill.

sources.title: AI a brand for Germany
sources.evidence: Champions German/European AI leadership and research investment, subject to ethical, legal and social constraints.

sources.title: BMJ: German MPs to vote on preimplantation genetic diagnosis
sources.evidence: Reports Merkel opposing embryo screening and allowing a conscience vote; concrete caution about reproductive biotechnology.

sources.title: Planeta Brasil: Liberdade
sources.date: 2026 edition listing; exact publication day not verified
sources.evidence: Brazilian publisher lists Liberdade by Angela Merkel and Beate Baumann; synopsis explicitly covers governing decisions and international politics. Search-index content was available; direct open failed.

sources.title: Kiepenheuer & Witsch: Freiheit
sources.evidence: Original publisher credits both Angela Merkel and Beate Baumann.

sources.title: Macmillan: Freedom
sources.evidence: English publisher gives subtitle Memoirs 1954–2021 and on-sale date; describes political decisions and diplomacy.

facts: 2006 reform devolved legislative competences; later pandemic required coordinated national measures.
estrutura.tension: Federal cooperation and national minimum rules, not secession or uniform central command.

facts: 2021 defence of free elections and parliamentary freedom; pandemic legislation remained reviewable by courts.
representacao.tension: Representative constitutional government, not direct popular assemblies or unelected technocracy.

facts: 2013 rejects indiscriminate surveillance; 2017 opposes recreational cannabis; 2021 supports curfews and vaccine obligations through law.
poder.tension: Civil liberties with proportionate security and public-health restrictions, not unlimited coercion.

facts: 2015 refugee protection accompanied by border administration and returns; 2016 integration stresses language and constitution.
imigracao.tension: Cultural coexistence and humanitarian welcome alongside civic integration; rejects both ethnic exclusion and unrestricted entry.

facts: 2021 supports NATO, European defence and deployed forces within multilateral diplomacy.
diplomacia.tension: Neither unilateral war nor disarmament pacifism; negotiations with credible defence.

facts: 2021 supports external deployments and UN mandate against terrorism.
intervencao.tension: Treaty-bound European influence and collective missions rather than unconditional neutrality or unilateral domination.

facts: 2014 social market combines private enterprise, unions and social insurance.
economia.tension: Private ownership and enterprise coexist with public responsibilities; neither collectivisation nor wholesale privatisation.

facts: 2014 fiscal restraint and minimum wage safeguards; 2020 exceptional EU debt/grants; 2019 ECB independence.
controle.tension: Ordoliberal rules plus crisis intervention; neither laissez-faire nor command economy.

facts: 2017 explicitly attacks protectionism as harmful to innovation.
comercio.tension: Open markets governed by common standards, not autarky or absence of all safeguards.

facts: 2017 affirms Christian roots and explicitly religiously neutral state protecting all faiths.
religiao.tension: Public value of religion without theocracy; personal Christianity does not imply discriminatory laws.

facts: 2017 opposes same-sex marriage but accepts gay adoption; supports respect after reform.
moral.tension: Traditional family ideal coexists with civil equality and gradual accommodation; not a blanket progressive or reactionary agenda.

facts: 2018 supports AI leadership under ethics; nuclear exit and earlier opposition to embryo selection show technological limits.
tecnologia.tension: Pro-innovation scientist with environmental and reproductive constraints, not transhumanist acceleration or rejection of industry.

limitations: Scope is chancellorship November 2005–December 2021, with later governing record weighted more. Later statements are not substituted for that historical profile. Research accessed 2026-10-01.

Some questions are Brazilian or speculative. Answer through analogous governing principles, not invented statements on Brazilian territorial groups, Amazon mining, cryptocurrency, implants or cultured meat. Moderate agreement/disagreement marks extrapolation; N only actual competing principles.
Coalition policy does not always equal personal preference. Individual marriage, embryo and cannabis statements distinguish Merkel from coalition compromises.
Nuclear exit is not opposition to AI or science; Christian faith is not theocracy; refugee reception is not rejection of language integration.
Brazilian publisher listing verifies title Liberdade without a subtitle; do not import a Portuguese-edition subtitle as though Brazilian.

recommendedMetadata.reason: Existing PT and EN accurately describe the historical chancellorship; communicated to coordinator before answering.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political memoir with Beate Baumann, covering governing and diplomatic decisions. Verified first publication 2024 and Brazilian publisher title; no existing entry to preserve.

processNotes.independence: Read only existing metadata, saved prompt, prior profilePeriod and source URLs; no old answers, vectors, similarities or score reports.
likelyNeighboursAndDistinctions: Christian democracy and social-market traditions of Kohl/Adenauer are plausible neighbours; Merkel differs through nuclear exit and 2015 refugee reception.
Macron shares European cooperation and market institutions, but Merkel has stronger explicit Christian/traditional-marriage commitments and federal institutions.
Cameron shares private-enterprise/fiscal-restraint positions, but Merkel endorses euro integration and organised social partnership. No neighbouring answers or vectors consulted.
